summary: Root-cause fix for INCIDENT_psv1_restart_wipes_sleeve_accounts_2026-09-26 (owner-delegated decision OWNER_DELEGATED_DECISION_engine_fix_2026-09-26.json decision[0]/[1]). (1) accounting.py: SleeveAccount.apply_recorded_funding(delta) — replay primitive whose sign convention was VERIFIED against the live apply_funding path (the ledger's per-decision funding_cashflow is the accounting convention: cash += delta, negative = cost paid — the dispatch context's '(positive = cost paid)' was inverted; every production cost book shares the default LONG_PAYS_POSITIVE_RATE convention so the recorded delta applies identically to every book; expected-equity identity asserted). SleeveAccount.apply_recorded_fill(...) — recorded-economics replay primitive that shares apply_fill's mutation core BIT-FOR-BIT via the extracted _apply_fill_mutation (same per-book economics, same cash mutation, same position bookkeeping, same identity assertion) but does NOT re-run the live admission guards. (2) executor.py: ForwardExecutor.recover_sleeve_from_ledger() -> dict: rebuilds the sleeve FRESH (idempotent, pure function of ledger bytes + cost books), replays rows in order (funding first, then fills — the live booking order, so fill-only rows reproduce recorded cash exactly), and enforces the VERIFICATION LAW per row (replayed cash vs recorded cash, abs diff <= 0.01). Divergences are disclosed as RECOVERY_DISCONTINUITY entries with two evidence-driven continuations: a diverging row that EXECUTED a rebalance is a LINEAGE BOUNDARY (the live book had been reset to a fresh account before it — reseed to the fresh account and re-apply the row; recorded cash trail re-verifies from there) while a diverging row with ZERO fills is the pure wipe artifact (fill truth kept, action TRUTH_KEPT). Any AccountingError during replay is recorded (kind FILL_REFUSED) without aborting; corrupt/partial ledgers raise LedgerCorruptError and the worker refuses to boot (fail closed). (3) shadow_worker.py build_executors: after constructing each executor, calls recover_sleeve_from_ledger() BEFORE any run_due and appends THE one deterministic recovery marker row via ledger.append_event only when fills_replayed > 0 or discontinuities exist: event_id = events.compute_event_id(family_id, arm_id, f'RECOVERY-{first ledger row scheduled_decision_utc}') (append-only anchor -> restart-idempotent, no duplicates; the frozen decision clock can never produce a RECOVERY-* stamp, and run_due's known_ids is ledger.event_ids, so the scheduler can never treat the marker as a decision). Marker carries scheduled_decision_utc (= anchor) for the ledger scans that max() on it (heartbeat _last_completed, scheduler.run_once/heartbeat) and schema psv1_sleeve_recovery@1 with the full recovery summary nested (no top-level cash/funding keys, so valuation.rebuild_positions reads it as a no-op). Families that never held anything (empty ledger; BANDRIDGE 67 rows zero fills; BASISLV DATA_BLOCKED-only) get NO marker. DEVIATION FROM DISPATCH (measured, disclosed): the dispatch suggested replaying fills via apply_fill(gross_cap_equity=None); the read-only dry-run on the REAL ledgers falsified that choice — per-row full-universe marks are not in the ledger, so the guards' gross check measured open positions at stale fill-ref marks and spuriously refused recorded shorts (XSECT would have 'recovered' to cash 17,033 vs its recorded 99,948 book; ILLIQ lost its XRP short). The recorded fills already passed admission live with decision-time marks and the start-of-rebalance basis; re-admission with degraded information re-litigates settled history and corrupts the very book being recovered. apply_recorded_fill keeps the guards' intent intact (refusals were enforced live, pre-mutation; the ledger is the record of what was lawfully admitted) and keeps the identity assertion. A second measured correction: the ledger itself records evidence of TWO flat-evidenced resets BEFORE the 2026-09-26 artifact (XSECT rows 2026-09-19 and 2026-09-25 both carry previous_weights {} and cash == 100,000 minus exactly that row's own rebalance costs), so a single-continuum replay would net the new lineage's fill quantities against the old book into garbage positions (cash continuity cannot catch it — cash mutations are position-independent); hence the lineage-boundary reseed rule.

known_limitations: Cost-book replay limitation (disclosed in code): replay recomputes fill economics with the CURRENT cost books; exact for every existing fill (XSECT/ILLIQ books never changed — per-fill recorded fee/slippage/fill_price re-verified against the current books to 1e-9; BANDRIDGE has zero fills). A future cost-regime change while positions are open would need regime-aware replay — out of scope, noted for the owner.

Live admission guards are NOT re-run on replay (apply_recorded_fill): measured on the real ledgers, re-running them on stale replay marks spuriously refuses recorded shorts. Guards were enforced live, pre-mutation; recovery trusts the append-only record. Invalid fills (bad side/qty/ref/tick) are still refused by the primitive and an identity-assert failure would be recorded as a FILL_REFUSED discontinuity without aborting.

Decision/order-intent counters and per-position funding_paid attribution are not reconstructible from the aggregate per-decision records; they restart at replay-derived values (funding_paid stays 0 on recovered positions). Informational only — sizing/caps/retire law never read them.

equity_after in the recovery summary is measured at the lineage's own fill-reference marks (per-row full-universe marks are not in the ledger); for the net-zero XSECT/ILLIQ books it equals the recorded cash to the cent, and the next live decision refreshes all marks via update_marks before sizing, so no decision ever sizes off stale marks.

The lineage-boundary reseed adopts the fresh-account basis with cash re-verifying exactly (cash mutations are position-independent); position reconstruction is faithful when the reset row is flat-evidenced (previous_weights == {} — true for BOTH real reset rows). A hypothetical reset row with non-empty previous_weights would re-anchor cash but best-effort positions, disclosed via flat_evidenced: false and verdict RECOVERED_WITH_DISCONTINUITIES.
